fields.reasoning: QA's cycle-3 finding was confirmed by its critic. ship-change.toml's render step stages only .rhiza/rendered. Builder actor records (recordAgentActor) stay uncommitted until land, so the PR head has rendered actor pages with no records, and this repo's CI make check fails before sign-off. Staging .rhiza/log in the same step is the smallest fix, and it matches what land already does (git add .rhiza). Changing the leaf instead would leave ship-change unable to ship in Rhiza's own repo, which is the change set's intent.
fields.statement: Ship-change's render step commits the worktree's uncommitted .rhiza/log entries together with .rhiza/rendered, so the branch it pushes holds every actor record its rendered pages are built from and rhiza check passes on a clone of it. A test proves it: a builder that commits only its own files, then rhiza check on a fresh clone of the pushed branch passes. Leaf ship-change-file keeps its scope and its statement names this.
